title: SQL for Customer Success Managers
learners: 12 customer success managers who use Looker daily and have never written SQL; evening workshop, 6 weekly 2-hour sessions

outcomes.text: Write a SELECT query with WHERE, ORDER BY and LIMIT that returns a requested slice of an accounts table
Calculate counts, sums and averages per customer segment using GROUP BY and HAVING
Combine accounts, usage and tickets tables with JOINs to answer a question that spans them
Translate a Looker explore (dimensions, measures, filters) into an equivalent SQL query
Diagnose a failing or wrong-result query from its error message or output and fix it
Build a multi-step query with CTEs that answers a real renewal-risk or health-score question and explain its logic to a colleague

modules.title: First queries: SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY
modules.activity: Guided queries on a practice accounts table; then pull 'enterprise accounts renewing this quarter, soonest first' unguided

assessment.evidence: three new data requests answered with working queries, checked against expected row counts

modules.title: Summarising: aggregates and GROUP BY
modules.activity: Rebuild three familiar Looker measures by hand, then compare the SQL Looker shows ('Show SQL') with your own

assessment.evidence: a per-segment summary query plus a short note mapping each Looker dimension, measure and filter to the matching SQL clause

modules.title: Joining tables
modules.activity: Join accounts to tickets, then add usage; inspect what changes between INNER and LEFT JOIN with row counts

assessment.evidence: a query answering 'which accounts have high ticket volume and falling usage' and a sentence justifying the join type chosen

modules.title: Debugging and sanity-checking
modules.activity: Six broken queries (syntax error, fan-out duplicates, wrong filter), with hints withdrawn over time

assessment.evidence: a diagnosis and fix for two unseen broken queries, each naming the cause and the evidence line or row count

modules.title: Multi-step questions with CTEs
modules.activity: Refactor a nested query into CTEs; pair-explain each step to a partner

assessment.evidence: a CTE-based draft of the capstone query, reviewed by a peer using the rubric

modules.title: Capstone: a renewal-risk query
modules.activity: Build and present a renewal-risk or health-score query on your own portfolio-style data; peer questions

assessment.evidence: final query plus a 3-minute walkthrough, scored on the rubric below

final.evidence: capstone renewal-risk query (uses filters, grouping and joins), a mapping back to the equivalent Looker explore, one bug found and fixed in a colleague's query, and a spoken walkthrough

levels: Query runs and returns the right rows; row counts were checked against a known figure
Query runs, but one filter or join gives duplicate or missing rows
Query errors or answers a different question
Walkthrough names what each CTE does and why each join type was chosen
Walkthrough describes the clauses but not the reasons
Walkthrough only reads the code aloud
